source_conversation.content: my iphone clock is an hour off since i got back from europe, how do i fix this

candidates.decision_basis: The user states iPhone and a wrong clock after travel, so the automatic date and time route from the iPhone passages applies directly.
candidates.target:
Set the date and time automatically on your iPhone:
1. Make sure that your device is connected to the internet.
2. Install the latest software updates for your device.
3. Open Settings, tap **General**, tap **Date & Time**, then turn on **Set Time Automatically**.
4. If a message says that updated time zone information is available, restart your device and any paired Apple Watch.
5. Open Settings, tap **Privacy & Security**, tap **Location Services**, scroll to the bottom and tap **System Services**, then turn on **Setting Time Zone**.
Set Time Automatically might not be available with all carriers or in all countries and regions. If the device has a Screen Time passcode or a corporate profile with device restrictions installed, the setting might be dimmed (grayed out).
candidates.author_note: Must cover internet connection, software updates, Set Time Automatically, the time zone update restart message, and Setting Time Zone under Location Services, plus the two conditions. Gap: the Open Settings lead-in for step 5 and the conditions are paraphrased from fetch answers.
